title: Farmers’ organisations call for protest on December 2 seeking better crop price

ai.summary: Farmer organisations in Haryana called for a protest on December 2 demanding higher crop prices, with sugarcane farmers rejecting a state price hike and bajra growers seeking MSP procurement.

facts.claim: Farmer organisations in Haryana called for a protest on December 2
facts.quote: Amid growing resentment among farmers in Haryana over “inadequate” prices for bajra and sugarcane, a joint front of farmer organisations has called for a demonstration in Kurukshetra on December 2, demanding remunerative prices for crops.

facts.claim: sugarcane farmers rejected a state price hike
facts.quote: sugarcane farmers have rejected the ₹15 per quintal hike announced by the State government this year, taking the price to ₹430 per quintal.
While bajra growers are demanding procurement at the announced minimum support price (MSP) of ₹2,900 per quintal

facts.claim: Haryana Kisan Congress organised a dharna
facts.quote: Extending support to bajra farmers, the Haryana Kisan Congress organised a day-long dharna at the new grain market in Charkhi Dadri, demanding procurement at MSP.

facts.claim: Congress Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Singh Surjewala alleged limited procurement at MSP
facts.quote: Addressing the gathering, Congress Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Singh Surjewala alleged that despite Haryana producing 1.3 million metric tonnes of bajra in 2025-26 and an estimated 1.5 million metric tonnes in 2026-27, government procurement at MSP had been limited to just 420 quintals.

facts.claim: Farmers were promised ₹600 compensation but received less
facts.quote: He said the BJP government had promised compensation of ₹600 per quintal under the “Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana”, assuring farmers that they would effectively receive ₹2,300 per quintal for their produce. However, farmers had been forced to sell bajra at ₹1,800-₹2,200 per quintal and had not received any compensation under the scheme, he alleged.
protesters demanded a sugarcane price of ₹600 per quintal in line with the Swaminathan Commission’s recommendations

ai.background_note: Haryana farmers are protesting low crop prices and rejected state price hikes, with demands for MSP procurement and higher sugarcane prices.
